faqs.question: How do I write a Navratri invitation for WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Put the event, the day and date, the start time and the place in one message of 20 to 45 words, then send a pinned location as a second message. End with a reply-by day and a line saying it is fine to say no, so people answer instead of going quiet.

faqs.question: How many days before should I send a Navratri puja invitation?
faqs.answer: Two to three days ahead suits a home aarti, a week suits a dandiya night with passes to buy, and the evening before suits a golu visit. Expect late replies anyway: in Raksha Bandhan 2026, our nearest measured festival, 49.4% of SubhSandesh pages were built on the festival day itself.

faqs.question: When is kanya pujan in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: In 2026 Durga Ashtami and Maha Navami fall on the same day, Monday 19 October, so most families hold kanya pujan that morning. In 2027 Ashtami is Thursday 7 October and Navami Friday 8 October, per Drik Panchang for New Delhi.

faqs.question: Who should I send a kanya pujan invitation to?
faqs.answer: Send it to the girls' parents, not to the girls. Give the time, the address and, above all, when you will drop each child home, then send a short reminder the night before.

faqs.question: Is it rude to invite elders to a Navratri puja by text?
faqs.answer: Many elders expect a phone call or an in-person invitation for a puja, and a forwarded text can read as an afterthought. Call first, then send the details as a text so they have the date, time and address written down.

faqs.question: How do I invite neighbours I barely know for Navratri?
faqs.answer: Message them directly with your flat number, the event, the date and time, and say there is nothing to bring. Research by Liu and colleagues (2023) found people underestimate how much others appreciate being reached out to, especially socially distant people, so the awkwardness is mostly on the sender's side.

faqs.question: What do you say in a golu invitation?
faqs.answer: Say the golu is up, give the days and the visiting window, such as 5 to 8 pm, and add your door number. A photo of the steps as a second message does most of the persuading.

faqs.question: Can I ask my crush to garba with a text message?
faqs.answer: Yes. Make it a question rather than an announcement: name the place and time, then ask if they will be your dandiya partner. If you want something they open and answer, the Be My Dandiya Partner page is built for one person.

faqs.question: Can I use the Be My Dandiya Partner page for a society or group invitation?
faqs.answer: No. It is a one-to-one invitation for a partner, a crush or a best friend as garba buddy, and its interface is in English. For a society, office or home-puja group, send a WhatsApp text with the five details instead.

faqs.question: Should a Navratri invitation say what to wear?
faqs.answer: Only for garba or dandiya, and in one line, such as "wear anything colourful" or the colour of the day. For a home puja or kanya pujan, leave dress out and spend the words on time and place.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Navratri Invitation Message: 14 Short Texts by Event and Guest

A good Navratri invitation message is 20 to 45 words long and names five things: the event, the day and date, the start time, the exact place, and how to reply. Most guests read it on a phone, where 48.3% of views of pages shared through SubhSandesh happen, so all five must fit one screen. Send it early, but expect late planners: in Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest festival we have measured, 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself (n = 89; our data, not Navratri data).

Sharad Navratri 2026 runs from Sunday 11 October to Monday 19 October, with Durga Ashtami and Maha Navami both on 19 October (Drik Panchang, New Delhi). In 2027 it begins on 30 September. Below: 14 original English texts for five events and four kinds of guest, a checklist and a format table.

## What should a Navratri invitation message include?

A Navratri invitation message should state the event and host, the day plus date, a start time, the place with a landmark, and a reply line. The blessing and the emoji are optional.

We counted the 80 English messages on the most visible list ranking for this search. They average 19.3 words, and not one gives a clock time, a date, a place or a way to reply. They are greetings dressed as invitations, so guests reply "what time, and where?"

1. **Event and host.** "Durga Maa's aarti at our place", not "Navratri celebrations".
2. **Day plus date.** "Thursday 15 October" survives forwarding; "this Thursday" does not.
3. **Start time, and an end time for garba.** Parents plan pickups around it.
4. **Place with a landmark.** Flat number, wing or gate, then a pinned location as a second message.
5. **A reply line with an easy out.** Give a reply-by day and say it is fine to say no.

A 2024 paper by Givi and Kirk in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology found that people who receive an invitation [overestimate how much declining it will upset the person who invited them](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/38079463) (we read the abstract only). It is about invitations in general, not Navratri, but it explains why "no worries if you can't" gets a quick answer instead of silence.

## Navratri invitation messages by event

Each event gets the same three fields: when to send, the message, and what to swap in. Dates are for 2026.

### 1. Home puja or aarti

- **Send:** two to three days before, to plan the prasad.
- **Swap in:** "falahari food for anyone fasting" if your guests keep the vrat.

> "Namaste! We're doing Durga Maa's aarti at home on Thursday 15 October at 7:30 pm, followed by prasad and dinner. Flat 402, Gulmohar Apartments, next to the temple gate. Please tell us by Tuesday if you can come, so we cook enough."

### 2. Kanya pujan

- **Send:** to the girls' parents at least two days ahead, then a reminder the night before. In 2026 Ashtami and Navami fall on the same day, Monday 19 October; in 2027 Ashtami is 7 October and Navami 8 October.
- **Swap in:** the pickup and drop line. Parents decide on that sentence more than any other.

> "Namaste ji, we're holding kanya pujan at home on Monday 19 October at 9 am and would be honoured if [daughter's name] could join. After the puja there's puri, chana and halwa, and we'll drop her home by 10:30. Could you confirm by Saturday?"

> "Just a reminder for tomorrow: kanya pujan at ours, 9 am. We're looking forward to seeing [name], and please don't bring anything."

### 3. Garba night

- **Send:** four to five days before, in the group chat plus a personal line to anyone new.

> "Garba on our terrace on Saturday 17 October, 8 pm till 10. Wear anything colourful; we'll have snacks at the break. B-wing terrace, Shanti Nagar. Reply with a headcount by Thursday!"

> "Hi Meera, I'd love you to come to our terrace garba on Saturday 17 October at 8 pm. It's small and beginner-friendly, so no need to know the steps. Shall I save you a spot?"

### 4. Dandiya night

- **Send:** a week before when passes are involved.
- **Swap in:** the pass price, only if they are paying their share.

> "Dandiya night with us on Sunday 18 October! We're booking passes for the society ground, 7:30 pm onwards. Bring your own sticks if you have a favourite pair. Can I count you in by Wednesday so I can get your pass?"

### 5. Golu

In South Indian homes a golu is a stepped display of dolls, and [women in the neighbourhood invite each other in the evenings to see it](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golu_(festival)). In a 2026 ethnography of households in Chidambaram, IIZUKA Mayumi records that [guests were asked to sing before the display, and that women gave tāmpūlam (betel leaves, areca nuts, turmeric and flowers) at the end of each visit](https://ousar.lib.okayama-u.ac.jp/files/public/7/70056/20260324155416599235/jdc_005_082.pdf).

- **Send:** the evening before.
- **Swap in:** a photo of the steps as a second message.

> "Hello Anjali, our golu is up, seven steps with my grandmother's dolls. Would you come over on Friday 16 October, any time from 5 to 8 pm, for sundal and a song? We're in C-12."

> "Golu is up! Drop in any evening till Monday 19 October, 5 to 8 pm. Bring the children; there's a new park set on the bottom step."

## Navratri invitation messages by recipient

The recipient changes the tone and the channel more than the event does, so each entry names the channel first. Dates are again for 2026.

### 6. Family and elders

- **Channel:** call first, then text the details.

> "Pranaam Mausi, as I said on the phone, the Ashtami puja is at our place on Monday 19 October at 10 am. Papa will pick you up at 9:15. Your blessings are the reason we're doing it, so please come."

> "Cousins' garba is back! Saturday 17 October, 8 pm at Nani's. Dress code: anything you can twirl in. Confirm in this group by Thursday."

### 7. Neighbours

- **Channel:** a direct message, not the building group, where an invite reads as a notice.

A 2023 paper by Liu, Rim, Min and Min in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology found, across preregistered experiments, that [people underestimate how much others appreciate being reached out to, and that the gap is larger between socially distant people](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/35816566) (abstract only). The neighbour you only nod to in the lift is that case.

> "Hi, we're your neighbours in 304. We're having a small aarti and dinner on Thursday 15 October at 7:30 pm and would be glad if your family could join. Nothing to bring. Do let us know by Tuesday?"

### 8. Friends

- **Channel:** the group for the plan, a personal message for the friend who ignores groups.

> "Navratri plan: garba at Riya's on Saturday 17 October, 8 pm, then late dinner. Thumbs up here by Thursday if you're in."

> "Garba buddy? I'm going to the Sector 5 ground at 8 pm most nights. Pick any two and I'll meet you at gate 2."

### 9. One special person

- **Channel:** a private message, at an hour they can answer.

> "I already know where I'll be on Saturday: the Sector 5 garba, 8 pm. I'd enjoy it a lot more with you as my dandiya partner. Will you come?"

This invitation is a question, not logistics. To ask with something they open and answer, the [Be My Dandiya Partner invitation page](https://subhsandesh.in/dandiya-partner) is built for exactly one person. You add nine short lines (one per night), up to six photos and the night's date, time, venue and dress code; they light nine diyas, play a dhol-beat game, pick the colour they'll twirl in, then answer "Will you be my Dandiya partner?"

It opens in a phone browser with no app or account and ends in a 1080×1920 Dandiya Pass, Instagram Story size. After five tries the No button turns into a second Yes. You can add a password, as 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators do before sharing.

## Text, card or page: which Navratri invitation format fits?

This compares the formats people actually send, by who they suit and what they carry. For a group, a plain text with the five details beats a card captioned only "Happy Navratri".

| Format | Suits | Carries date, time, venue? | Our number |
|---|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp text (this page) | family, neighbours, friends' groups | Yes, in 25–45 words | 48.3% of shared-page views are on a phone |
| Image card | 20+ guests, society events | Only if the caption repeats them | 0 of 80 top-list messages gave a time or place |
| Be My Dandiya Partner page | one person | Yes, plus Add to calendar | 9 lines, 6 photos, Yes after 5 No taps |
| Same-day reminder text | anyone who has not replied | Yes, in one line | 49.4% of rakhi pages were built on the day (n = 89) |

## When a Navratri invitation text is the wrong choice

A text is the wrong opener for elders who expect a call or a visit. Ring first, then send the details.

For 50 or more guests, a WhatsApp thread loses the headcount; use a form or the society's pass system. Our page is the wrong tool for any group invite: it is one-to-one, and the sender gets a single email, the first time their one recipient says yes.

Its interface is English, so for guests who read Hindi or Gujarati first, text them in their language. It sells no garba passes and finds no one a partner.

If the plan goes beyond garba night, [The Invitation page](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) suits better: a yes turns into a countdown, and on the day the plan unlocks one stop at a time. Hindi wording, organisers' garba cards, dandiya-night messages, office invitations and free card makers each have their own guide.

## Sources

- Givi and Kirk (2024), "Saying no: The negative ramifications from invitation declines are less severe than we think," *Journal of Personality and Social Psychology*. Abstract only.
- Liu, Rim, Min and Min (2023), "The surprise of reaching out: Appreciated more than we think," *Journal of Personality and Social Psychology*. Abstract only.
- IIZUKA Mayumi (2026), "Generating Sacredness in the Domestic Sphere: Wedding Rituals and the Navarātri Kolu Festival in South India," *Dynamics of Civilizations* 5: 82–100. Full text read.
- Drik Panchang, [Sharad Navratri dates](https://www.drikpanchang.com/navratri/ashwin-shardiya-navratri-dates.html?geoname-id=1261481&year=2026), New Delhi, checked for 2026 and 2027. Undated.
- SubhSandesh first-party data, measured 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-09.

failed.why: Structural. Givi & Kirk 2024 (invitees overestimate the cost of declining) carries the reply-line advice and Liu et al. 2023 (reaching out is appreciated more than senders expect) carries the neighbours entry; both are general invitation/contact psychology, so either could sit unchanged in garba-invitation-wording or dandiya-night-invitation-message. auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over the five pages analysed: it is the only one whose texts each carry a date, time, place and reply line, the only one covering kanya pujan and golu invitations with Drik Panchang-checked 2026 and 2027 dates, and it prints a measured gap (0 of 80 leading-list messages give a time or place) plus first-party phone-open data no rival has. It cannot overcome tring.co.in's domain authority, the SERP was US-served so India positions are unknown, its two psychology sources are generic to any invitation post, and the messages are copyable, so the moat is the checklist, dates and data rather than the wording.
